headline_marked: NCP convoy [[attacked with stones twice in Sylhet]]; Sarjis Alam blames BNP
headline: NCP convoy attacked with stones twice in Sylhet; Sarjis Alam blames BNP
summary: Vehicles were vandalized during the party's 'July March' program, with the rear windscreen of Sarjis Alam's car smashed. The party blames BNP activists for the attacks.
details: A motorcade carrying National Citizen Party (NCP) leaders was attacked with brickbats in Sylhet's Golapganj on Thursday. The attack occurred near the Chowmuhani intersection after leaders left a meeting with families of those killed in the July Uprising.
The rear windscreen of the vehicle carrying Sarjis Alam, the party's chief organiser for the northern region, was smashed. An autorickshaw in the convoy was also damaged during the incident.
Local NCP leaders and Sarjis Alam blamed BNP activists for the attacks, with Sarjis describing the incident on Facebook as a "bloody attack" by "BNP criminals".
Sarjis Alam further claimed that the convoy was attacked a second time at Sylhet's Panchmile Bazar, reporting that vehicles were vandalized.
According to Md Sabed Ali, chief of Golapganj Police Station, bricks were thrown from a distance as the convoy was leaving the programme.
This incident follows a similar attack on the NCP's 'July March' in Habiganj on Tuesday evening.
Law-enforcing agencies arrived at the scene shortly after the attack to bring the situation under control.
caption:
NCP leaders' convoy was attacked twice in Sylhet with brickbats, smashing car windows. Sarjis Alam blames BNP activists.

A motorcade carrying National Citizen Party (NCP) leaders was attacked with brickbats in Sylhet's Golapganj on Thursday. The attack occurred near the Chowmuhani intersection after leaders left a meeting with families of those killed in the July Uprising.

The rear windscreen of the vehicle carrying Sarjis Alam, the party's chief organiser for the northern region, was smashed. An autorickshaw in the convoy was also damaged during the incident.

Local NCP leaders and Sarjis Alam blamed BNP activists for the attacks, with Sarjis describing the incident on Facebook as a "bloody attack" by "BNP criminals".

Sarjis Alam further claimed that the convoy was attacked a second time at Sylhet's Panchmile Bazar, reporting that vehicles were vandalized.

According to Md Sabed Ali, chief of Golapganj Police Station, bricks were thrown from a distance as the convoy was leaving the programme.

This incident follows a similar attack on the NCP's 'July March' in Habiganj on Tuesday evening.

Law-enforcing agencies arrived at the scene shortly after the attack to bring the situation under control.

headline_marked: Tk 10mn dowry case: [[Prince Mamun's bail rejected]] by Dhaka court
headline: Tk 10mn dowry case: Prince Mamun's bail rejected by Dhaka court
summary: The social media star is accused of beating his wife, model Atqiya Faizah Mohona, after demanding a massive dowry sum.
details: A Dhaka court has rejected the bail application of social media star Abdullah Al Mamun, known as Prince Mamun, in a case involving the beating of his wife for a dowry of Tk 10 million.
The court decision followed a hearing on Thursday where the plaintiff, Atqiya Faizah Mohona, appeared to oppose the bail request.
According to the case, Mamun demanded Tk 10 million to open a shop and physically and mentally abused Mohona when she refused to pay.
The plaintiff alleges that Mamun, in an intoxicated state, indiscriminately punched, kicked, and tried to strangle her, leaving her with a bloody wound under her left eye and bruises on her ear.
The couple had been married for only five months. Mohona testified in court that she had been tortured throughout this short period.
Mamun's lawyers argued that the two had a mutual fight and that no medical certificate was attached to the case, while also mentioning disputes involving a third party.
Mamun is also facing a separate case for attempting suicide during a Facebook Live broadcast on July 23, where he tried to hang himself from a ceiling fan.
caption:
A social media star's demand for Tk 10 million in dowry ends in court.

A Dhaka court has rejected the bail application of social media star Abdullah Al Mamun, known as Prince Mamun, in a case involving the beating of his wife for a dowry of Tk 10 million.

The court decision followed a hearing on Thursday where the plaintiff, Atqiya Faizah Mohona, appeared to oppose the bail request.

According to the case, Mamun demanded Tk 10 million to open a shop and physically and mentally abused Mohona when she refused to pay.

The plaintiff alleges that Mamun, in an intoxicated state, indiscriminately punched, kicked, and tried to strangle her, leaving her with a bloody wound under her left eye and bruises on her ear.

The couple had been married for only five months. Mohona testified in court that she had been tortured throughout this short period.

Mamun's lawyers argued that the two had a mutual fight and that no medical certificate was attached to the case, while also mentioning disputes involving a third party.

Mamun is also facing a separate case for attempting suicide during a Facebook Live broadcast on July 23, where he tried to hang himself from a ceiling fan.
